## [Retro Game Reviews: Barakel: The Fallen Angel (Nokia N-Gage review)](https://www.retrogamesreview.co.uk/2025/05/barakel-fallen-angel-nokia-n-gage-review.html)
Published: 2025-05-21T00:00:00.000Z

## Wednesday, 21 May 2025

### Barakel: The Fallen Angel (Nokia N-Gage review) 

Developer: StormBASIC Games Publisher: Nokia, Technobubble Entertainment Released: 2004 

### Barakel: The Fallen Angel is a hack and slash game that was only released in Portugal and Spain.

+ Supports local multiplayer and a nice feature is how friends can share objects, gold and potions to keep inventories stocked.

+ Does a very good job of signposting you to your next objective, both with in-game arrows and via menu reminders.

- Has severe glitches, including a consistent game-breaking crash shortly after the third boss due to a memory overflow issue.

- Saving your game costs too much currency and the risk of losing tons of progress makes farming a boringly stressful necessity.

- Despite enemies typically swarming in groups, your attacks can only hit one at a time, leaving the other foe to freely drain your life bar.

- Limited field-of-view can make it hard to see the exact location of NPCs, as well as the placement of switches in dungeon areas.

- Features an egregious amount of typos from the outset, which does ruin the immersion and gives the game an unpolished feel.

# Barakel: The Fallen Angel (N-Gage Game Review)

 Date: 2021-03-04 Author: Bohdan Dovhaliuk 0 Comments 

There was such a milestone in the history of N-Gage as localized games. Their bandle releases, as you guessed, were in specific countries. The sale was performing by the distribution of cartridges without covers and instructions.

Our hero, for example, was released purely for the Spanish market. It happened in 2004. That’s how lucky people at that time in Ibiza could have fun in the evenings under Benny Benassi’s sets and in the day to savor one of the best mobile RPG games of the year.

...

## Graphics

3D graphics and a third-person view from above allow you to enjoy the vast game world in full. There are also good texture details, which give the picture vividness and saturation.

The models of characters and drawings of their avatars look pretty well. It applies to huge trolls, knights, orcs, and more.

## Soundtrack

In such a belligerent game like Barakel, even music is militant. Epic melodies alternate with calmer yet more mysterious notes. Therefore, the atmosphere of this game for Nokia N-Gage was support on excellent level thanks to the presented songs.

Besides, my ears are delighted with realistic sound effects, for example, during battles. This is an important point because you have to spend the lion’s share of time in them.

## Story

Traditionally for RPG mobile games, here we get a fascinating story. Archangel Barakel was exiled to earth and forced to find ways to get back. To get to heaven, he must fight the evil of the world.

The events begin at the entrance to the village of Norham, which has recently suffered a crushing invasion. We find out about what happened to the surviving villagers and the road searching for by Barakel.

Many obstacles and unexpected turns await him ahead. And in all this, of course, we’ve got his human body covered.

## Gameplay

The control is very comfortable and intuitive. The combat system is simple, and there are no lags. This allows you to watch the battles as if from your window without slowdowns.

The battle action looks exciting, and the process takes a long time. I started to want it more and more. However, the equipment will have to be updated every time because it can wear out in battle.

By the way, the number of dialogs is very modest as for one of the best mobile RPG. Whether it’s a good thing is a subjective question. Some people like to read a lot and get into the story, while others prefer the dynamic process.

An interesting feature of the game is the ability to play it together with friends, thanks to the multiplayer. To do this, you need to connect the devices via Bluetooth. Once connected, you can exchange items and gold among yourselves.

## [SIS File Format](https://www.thouky.co.uk/software/psifs/sis.html)

# SIS File Format

 Version 1.19, 19-Nov-24 by Alexander Thoukydides (`alex@thouky.co.uk`)

...

## Introduction

 The EPOC operating system uses files with a `.SIS` extension to allow easy installation of applications. These are usually produced using the `makesis` tool, and are handled by either the control panel `Add/remove` program or EPOC Connect. This document attempts to provide sufficient information to allow other software to be written that can decode and use SIS files. 

 The format of SIS files was changed in the Symbian OS version 9.1 release of Software Install. This document describes the original format used by earlier versions. Information about the restructured and redesigned format can be found at http://www.symbian.com/developer/techlib/papers/SymbianOSv91/softwareinstallsis.pdf. 

 The latest version of this document will normally be available from https://www.thouky.co.uk/software/psifs/sis.html.

...

### Sections

 SIS files consist of the following sections: 

| Section |
| --- |
| File Header |
| Language Records |
| File Records |
| Requisite Records |
| Component Name Record |
| Capabilities Record |
| Certificates Record |
| Resource Data |

 The sections are stored contiguously, without any padding or alignment. They should also normally be in the order listed, otherwise the residual SIS files may be larger than necessary.

...

## File Header

 All SIS files start with a standard header: 

| Offset | | Bytes | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0x00` | 0 | 4 | UID 1 |
| `0x04` | 4 | 4 | UID 2 |
| `0x08` | 8 | 4 | UID 3 |
| `0x0c` | 12 | 4 | UID 4 |
| `0x10` | 16 | 2 | Checksum |
| `0x12` | 18 | 2 | Number of languages |
| `0x14` | 20 | 2 | Number of files |
| `0x16` | 22 | 2 | Number of requisites |
| `0x18` | 24 | 2 | Installation language |
| `0x1a` | 26 | 2 | Installation files |
| `0x1c` | 28 | 2 | Installation drive |
| `0x1e` | 30 | 2 | Number of capabilities |
| `0x20` | 32 | 4 | Installer version |
| `0x24` | 36 | 2 | Options |
| `0x26` | 38 | 2 | Type |
| `0x28` | 40 | 2 | Major version |
| `0x2a` | 42 | 2 | Minor version |
| `0x2c` | 44 | 4 | Variant |
| `0x30` | 48 | 4 | Languages pointer |
| `0x34` | 52 | 4 | Files pointer |
| `0x38` | 56 | 4 | Requisites pointer |
| `0x3c` | 60 | 4 | Certificates pointer |
| `0x40` | 64 | 4 | Component name pointer |

 The header of EPOC release 6 format SIS files is extended: 

| Offset | | Bytes | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0x44` | 68 | 4 | Signature pointer |
| `0x48` | 72 | 4 | Capabilities pointer |
| `0x4C` | 76 | 4 | Installed space |
| `0x50` | 80 | 4 | Maximum installed space |
| `0x54` | 84 | 16 | Reserved |

 The UID 1, UID 2 and UID 3 fields are the first three words of the file, and indicate the type of data it contains. UID 1 is the UID of the application to be installed, or `0x10000000` if none. UID 2 is `0x1000006D` for EPOC releases 3, 4 and 5, and `0x10003A12` for EPOC release 6. UID 3 is always `0x10000419`.

...

The Installation language and Installation files fields are both initially zero. When the SIS file is installed, these are modified with the settings used for the installation. 

 The Installation drive field is initially `0x0000` for EPOC releases 3, 4 and 5, and `0x0021` (the character code for "`!`") for EPOC release 6. When the SIS file is installed, this is modified with the setting used for the installation. 

 The Installer version field specifies the version of the `Add/remove` program required to handle the file. This is normally 68 (`0x00000044`) or 100 (`0x00000064`) for EPOC releases 3, 4 and 5, and 200 (`0x000000c8`) for EPOC release 6.

...

The Type may be any of the following: 

| Type | Code | | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0x0000` | `SA` | `SISAPP` | Contains an application (the default) |
| `0x0001` | `SY` | `SISSYSTEM` | Contains a shared/system component such as a DLL or OPX (EPOC release 6) |
| `0x0002` | `SO` | `SISOPTION` | Contains an optional component, independently selectable by the user (EPOC release 6) |
| `0x0003` | `SC` | `SISCONFIG` | Configures an existing application or service (EPOC release 6) |
| `0x0004` | `SP` | `SISPATCH` | Patches an existing component (EPOC release 6) |
| `0x0005` | `SU` | `SISUPGRADE` | Upgrades an existing component (EPOC release 6) |

...

If the File record type field at the start of the record is `0x00000000` or `0x00000001` then the record specifies a single file to be installed.

...

| `0x1c` | 28 | 4 n | File length(s) |
| `0x1c` + 4 n | 28 + 4 n | 4 n | File pointer(s) |

 The file records of EPOC release 6 format SIS files are extended: 

| Offset | | Bytes | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0x1c` + 8 n | 28 + 8 n | 4 n | Original file length(s) |
| `0x1c` + 12 n | 28 + 12 n | 4 | MIME type length |
| `0x20` + 12 n | 32 + 12 n | 4 | MIME type pointer |

 The File type consists of one of the following types: 

| File type | | Code | | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0x00` | 0 | `FF` | `FILE` | Standard file (the default) |
| `0x01` | 1 | `FT` | `FILETEXT` | Text file to display during installation |
| `0x02` | 2 | | | SIS component file |
| `0x03` | 3 | `FR` | `FILERUN` | File to be run during installation and/or removal |
| `0x04` | 4 | `FN` | `FILENULL` | File does not yet exist, but will be created when the application is run |
| `0x05` | 5 | `FM` | `FILEMIME` | Open file |

...

## Requisite Records

 The Requisites pointer field in the header points to the requisites records that specify the files that are required by the component being installed. The Number of requisites field in the header specifies the number of records. These are stored contiguously in the following format: 

| Offset | | Bytes | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0x00` | 0 | 4 | UID |
| `0x04` | 4 | 2 | Major version |
| `0x06` | 6 | 2 | Minor version |
| `0x08` | 8 | 4 | Variant |
| `0x0c` | 12 | 4 n | Requisite name length(s) |
| `0x0c` + 4 n | 12 + 4 n | 4 n | Requisite name pointer(s) |

 The UID field specifies the UID of the component that is required, i.e. the first word of its residual SIS file.

...

## Installation

 Installation of an SIS file requires several steps to be performed. These are described in the following sections. 

 These operations need to be repeated for any embedded component SIS files. 

### Select Language

 SIS files may support more than one language, as indicated by the Number of languages field in the header and the language records. The control panel `Add/remove` program attempts to use the current language of the machine, but EPOC Connect prompts the user to choose from the available options. 

### Check Requisites

 The requisite records specify a list of other components that need to be installed. The residual SIS files on the target machine should be searched to verify that a suitable version of the required component has been installed. 

### Check Previous Version

 The residual SIS files on the target machine are used to check for any previous versions of the application being installed. Any previous installation needs to be removed before installing the new version. 

 If the previous version is older than the version being installed then it is replaced without warning. However, if the previous version is newer then the behaviour depends on the installation program; the control panel `Add/remove` program requires the user to first uninstall the more recent version, but EPOC Connect displays a confirmation prompt to allow the existing application to be removed and replaced. 

### Copy Files

 The file records should be processed in the reverse of the order that they are stored in the SIS file. Text files should be displayed and component SIS files installed as they are encountered. 

 SIS files sometimes allow the user to select the installation drive. This is indicated by the destination file names having an exclamation mark ("`!`") specified as the drive letter. In this case the user should be prompted to select from the available drives. 

 Directories should be created automatically to accommodate files being copied. 

### Residual SIS File

 A residual SIS file is created in the `C:\System\Install\` directory on the target machine. This allows the control panel to display a list of installed programs, and provides the dependency information required for removing the component or installing other applications. 

 The main modification is that the file is truncated after the file name and component name strings. This usually means that the file data is omitted, but this relies upon the SIS file contents being in a sensible order. 

 Finally, three fields in the header are modified with the settings used for the installation. The Installation language field is set to the language selected for the installation, the Installation files field is set to the number of files installed, and the Installation drive field is set to the drive letter where the files were installed.

This document describes the newly restructured and redesigned SIS file format, which is introduced to 
complement the Symbian OS v9.1 release of Software Install. SIS files are used as the primary means of 
packaging files for deployment to a device, and are interpreted accordingly by the native software 
installer. As well as simply containing files, the SIS file can contain conditional statements which 
influence the installation e.g. device specific installations, language-specific installations, and user 
selectable optional components. 
Symbian OS v9.1 delivers new security features to the device, so operations which were previously 
possible via software install may now no-longer be possible. In addition, the device-side native installer is 
now policing the installation to ensure that the package meets certain security criteria before installation 
can succeed.

...

#### 2.1 Overview

The information in the SIS file is split up into two separate parts. The first part is the meta-data, 
describing the files that need to be installed. The second part of the SIS file contains all the actual file 
data. This enables software installation to be split into two phases, a decision and an installation phase. 
During the decision phase, the SIS file is examined and security checks are carried out in order to verify 
the install. The installation phase is only carried out if the verification is successful and is the process of 
copying the files to the device.

fields, for example, fields employing bit-indicators such as TInstallFlags.

# `DumpSIS` - Installation file decompiler 

## Purpose

 `DumpSIS` is a PC-based utility which decompiles a SIS file. 

 The input to `DumpSIS` is a v9.x SIS file. Its output is the corresponding package file and (optionally) the source files. `CreateSIS` can be run on the resultant files to recreate the SIS file. When run on pre-v9.x SIS files, `DumpSIS` reports an error. 

 `DumpSIS` is found in the standard tools location, `\epoc32\tools\`. 

## Syntax

`> DumpSIS [-i] [-v] [-h] [-x] [-l[-y]][-d directory]
 filename.sis`

 where: 

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-i` | displays verbose output |
| `-v` | displays the `DumpSIS` version number |
| `-h` | displays help |
| `-x` | extracts the files |
| `-d` | specifies the directory to which the files are extracted, creating it if necessary. By default, files are extracted to a directory with the same as the SIS file. |
| `-p` | pauses before finishing. |
| `-l` | lists the executables and their capabilities. It also verifies that the capabilities listed in the SIS file are the same as those in the executable(s). |
| `-y` | lists the executables and their capabilities, in the format supported by the `DumpInstallFileStatus` tool. This option must be specified with the `-l` option. |

## Notes 

- The source-filenames specified in the original package file are not stored in the SIS file so `DumpSIS` invents names for the extracted files. 
- `DumpSIS` does not reinstate timestamps. 
- If the SIS file is signed, you can display and strip the signatures with `SignSIS`; `DumpSIS` makes no attempt to preserve or display any signing information.

## [Sisopen - epoc and symbian file extraction utility - antirez weblog](https://oldblog.antirez.com/page/sisopen)

## Sisopen - epoc and symbian file extraction utility

## Sisopen

Sisopen is a tool to list and extract the content of SIS files. SIS files are installation files used in Symbian-based smartphones like many S60 Nokia phones. Sisopen is an ANSI-C program, mainly targetted to Linux and other Unix-like systems it can be compiled almost in every system with a C compiler having zlib.

Defining NOZLIB at compile time makes you able to compile without zlib, but only file listing is available in this mode, files can't be extracted.

### EXAMPLE

First example, list the content of a .sis file

```
$ sisopen sis/torch.sissis/torch.sis: SIS header detected
  application UID: 0x78F172C
  application version: 1.20Languages
  UK English Files
000   !:\system\apps\Torch\Torch.aif                                        1941
001   !:\system\apps\Torch\Torch_caption.rsc                                  32
002   !:\system\apps\Torch\Torch.rsc                                          70
003   !:\system\apps\Torch\Torch.app                                        5548

```

A more interesting example showing the ability of sisopen to fully understand SIS files including conditionals:

```
$ sisopen sis/Nokia_N70_patch.SISsis/Nokia_N70_patch.SIS: SIS header detected
  application UID: 0x20000BB0
  application version: 1.00Languages
  UK English Files
[endif]
001 f C:\DOCUME~1\m1smith\LOCALS~1\Temp\MKS0\WrongDevice0.txt                122
[else]
003 f C:\DOCUME~1\m1smith\LOCALS~1\Temp\MKS0\Finished0.txt                   254
004 c C:\system\temp\NokiaN70Patch1.exe                                     1552
005 f C:\DOCUME~1\m1smith\LOCALS~1\Temp\MKS0\Distribution0.txt               288
[if (0x10200f9a == MachineUID)]

```

SIS file conditionals must be read upside down, starting from the bottom of the output. This is a patch for the N70 smartphone so the conditional is if MachineUID == 0x... (the N70 UID) install the files, else show a Wrong Device message.

### FEATURES

Sisopen is able to:

- list SIS file content, including conditionals, file type, installation time options
- extract files (try -x)
- the verbose mode gives a lot more information about the sis header and individual files (try -v)

## [SIS/SISX package extraction, E32Image binary analysis ...](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/3612)
Published: 2026-10-14T18:47:32.000Z

## Summary

Symbian OS (spanning EPOC, Series 60 / S60 v1-v5, UIQ, Series 80, and Symbian^3 / Anna / Belle) powers a vast historical ecosystem of mobile software, utilities, games, and enterprise tools. While official online services and vendor signing portals have ceased operations, the Symbian platform remains actively analyzed in retro-computing, digital preservation, embedded systems research, and mobile software forensics.

Currently, REA has no support for Symbian application containers, binary formats, or OS-specific C++ conventions. This feature introduces dedicated static reverse engineering capabilities for Symbian OS applications: unpacking `.sis` and `.sisx` package archives, parsing and loading E32Image executables/DLLs in Ghidra and Rizin, and reconstructing Symbian-specific architectural idioms (Cleanup Stack, Active Objects, Descriptors, and Capability security manifests).

### 1. Package Unpacking & Manifest Analysis (.sis and .sisx)

- Legacy SIS (Symbian v6–v8.x): Parse EPOC SIS archive headers, file records, language tables, and target drive mappings (`!:\system\apps\`).
- SISX / SIS9 (Symbian OS v9+):

- Parse the PKCS#7 signed SISX container, extracting embedded certificates, signatures, and trust chains.
- Extract package metadata: Package UID, Vendor Name, Target Device / S60 SDK compatibility ranges, and localized install manifests.
- Extract target file trees (e.g. `!:\sys\bin\*.exe`, `!:\resource\apps\*.rsc`, `!:\private\ \`).
- Map Capability Manifests: parse declared capabilities (e.g. `NetworkServices`, `LocalServices`, `ReadUserData`, `WriteUserData`, `UserEnvironment`, `DiskAdmin`, `AllFiles`, `TCB`) required by the application.

### 2. E32Image Executable & DLL Analysis (EPOC32)

- E32 Header & Metadata Parsing:

- Extract UID1 (binary type: EXE, DLL), UID2 (interface/category), and UID3 (application identifier).
- Extract Secure ID (SID), Vendor ID (VID), and runtime capability bitmasks.
- Identify target CPU architecture: ARM (ARMv5TE, ARMv6) and x86 emulator builds (WINS/WINSCW).
- Decompression: Support native decompression of Byte-Pair Compressed (BPC / inflate) E32 images to produce raw code and data sections.
- Import / Export Resolution:

- Symbian links by ordinal rather than function name. Implement ordinal-to-symbol mapping tables for core Symbian OS shared libraries (`euser.dll`, `apparc.dll`, `cone.dll`, `eikcore.dll`, `avkon.dll`, `bafl.dll`, `efsrv.dll`).
- Resolve import address tables (IAT) and virtual function table (vtable) layouts.
- Headless Provider Integration: Automatically load unpacked E32 binaries into Ghidra and Rizin with accurate base addresses, section relocations, and system library ordinal annotations.

...

### 4. Resource & Graphical Asset Extraction

- Compiled Resource Files (.rsc): Parse binary resource files (`.rsc`, `.r01`, `.r02`, etc.) containing UI dialogs, menu bars, strings, and localized application text.
- Image Containers (.mif and .mbm): Extract multi-bitmap (`.mbm`) and multi-image vector/SVG (`.mif`) icons and graphics.
- Application Information Files (.aif): Parse legacy AIF containers to extract app captions and icon bitmaps.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Introduce `analyze_symbian_application` in REA CLI and MCP contracts, accepting `.sis`, `.sisx`, `.app`, and `.exe` inputs.
2. Accurately unpack file entries and report declared capabilities from S60 v3/v5 `.sisx` packages.
3. Decompress and parse BPC-compressed E32Image binaries into valid ELF/raw sections with resolved core ordinals in Ghidra/Rizin.
4. Reconstruct Active Object event loops and identify `CActive::RunL` callbacks in structured evidence.
5. Provide unit and regression tests with synthetic/open-source Symbian test fixtures.

## [SIS File Format](https://www.thouky.co.uk/software/psifs/sis.html)

# SIS File Format

 Version 1.19, 19-Nov-24 by Alexander Thoukydides (`alex@thouky.co.uk`) 

> Copyright © Alexander Thoukydides. Permission is granted to copy, distribute and/or modify this document under the terms of the GNU Free Documentation License, Version 1.1 or any later version published by the Free Software Foundation; with no Invariant Sections, no Front-Cover Texts and no Back-Cover Texts. A copy of the license is included in the section entitled " GNU Free Documentation License". 

## Introduction

 The EPOC operating system uses files with a `.SIS` extension to allow easy installation of applications. These are usually produced using the `makesis` tool, and are handled by either the control panel `Add/remove` program or EPOC Connect. This document attempts to provide sufficient information to allow other software to be written that can decode and use SIS files. 

 The format of SIS files was changed in the Symbian OS version 9.1 release of Software Install. This document describes the original format used by earlier versions. Information about the restructured and redesigned format can be found at http://www.symbian.com/developer/techlib/papers/SymbianOSv91/softwareinstallsis.pdf. 

 The latest version of this document will normally be available from https://www.thouky.co.uk/software/psifs/sis.html.

...

- Jochen Siegenthaler's document providing a partial description of the SIS file format. 
- EPOC C++ SDK, Evaluation Edition. 
- Neuon's nSISUtil. 
- Analysis of a large selection of existing SIS files. 
- Andrew de Quincey's `xmakesis` Perl script, as updated by Rudolf Koenig. 
- Trial and error while developing PsiFS for RISC OS computers. 
- Corrections supplied by Dalibor Jelinek, Eberhard Mattes, Neil Masson, Stephanie Freitag, Bruno Tiago Rodrigues, Jimmy Shah, Jordan Walters, David Berry, Ren Yantao, a1z0r, Luca Cassioli, Wellu Mäkinen, Marcio Faustino and Tero Suomela.

...

### Sections

 SIS files consist of the following sections: 

| Section |
| --- |
| File Header |
| Language Records |
| File Records |
| Requisite Records |
| Component Name Record |
| Capabilities Record |
| Certificates Record |
| Resource Data |

 The sections are stored contiguously, without any padding or alignment. They should also normally be in the order listed, otherwise the residual SIS files may be larger than necessary.

...

## File Header

 All SIS files start with a standard header: 

| Offset | | Bytes | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0x00` | 0 | 4 | UID 1 |
| `0x04` | 4 | 4 | UID 2 |
| `0x08` | 8 | 4 | UID 3 |
| `0x0c` | 12 | 4 | UID 4 |
| `0x10` | 16 | 2 | Checksum |
| `0x12` | 18 | 2 | Number of languages |
| `0x14` | 20 | 2 | Number of files |
| `0x16` | 22 | 2 | Number of requisites |
| `0x18` | 24 | 2 | Installation language |
| `0x1a` | 26 | 2 | Installation files |
| `0x1c` | 28 | 2 | Installation drive |
| `0x1e` | 30 | 2 | Number of capabilities |
| `0x20` | 32 | 4 | Installer version |
| `0x24` | 36 | 2 | Options |
| `0x26` | 38 | 2 | Type |
| `0x28` | 40 | 2 | Major version |
| `0x2a` | 42 | 2 | Minor version |
| `0x2c` | 44 | 4 | Variant |
| `0x30` | 48 | 4 | Languages pointer |
| `0x34` | 52 | 4 | Files pointer |
| `0x38` | 56 | 4 | Requisites pointer |
| `0x3c` | 60 | 4 | Certificates pointer |
| `0x40` | 64 | 4 | Component name pointer |

...

The Files pointer field in the header points to the file records that specify the details of the files to be installed. The Number of Files field in the header specifies the number of records. These are stored contiguously, in the reverse of the order required for installation. Each record starts with a 4 byte File record type field specifying the type of record that follows:

...

If the File record type field at the start of the record is `0x00000000` or `0x00000001` then the record specifies a single file to be installed. It is in the following format: 

| Offset | | Bytes | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0x00` | 0 | 4 | File record type |
| `0x04` | 4 | 4 | File type |
| `0x08` | 8 | 4 | File details |
| `0x0c` | 12 | 4 | Source name length |
| `0x10` | 16 | 4 | Source name pointer |
| `0x14` | 20 | 4 | Destination name length |
| `0x18` | 24 | 4 | Destination name pointer |
| `0x1c` | 28 | 4 n | File length(s) |
| `0x1c` + 4 n | 28 + 4 n | 4 n | File pointer(s) |

 The file records of EPOC release 6 format SIS files are extended:

...

| `0x1c` + 8 n | 28 + 8 n | 4 n | Original file length(s) |

...

| `0x20` + 12 n | 32

...

The File type consists of one of the following types: 

| File type | | Code | | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0x00` | 0 | `FF` | `FILE` | Standard file (the default) |
| `0x01` | 1 | `FT` | `FILETEXT` | Text file to display during installation |
| `0x02` | 2 | | | SIS component file |
| `0x03` | 3 | `FR` | `FILERUN` | File to be run during installation and/or removal |
| `0x04` | 4 | `FN` | `FILENULL` | File does not yet exist, but will be created when the application is run |
| `0x05` | 5 | `FM` | `FILEMIME` | Open file |

...

The Requisites pointer field in the header points to the requisites records that specify the files that are required by the component being installed.

...

## Resource Data

 The remainder of the SIS file consists of the data referenced from the other sections. This is stored uncompressed and unpadded, usually in the following order: 

| Section |
| --- |
| String Block, containing: File Names Requisite Name Component Name |
| Code Block |
| Signature Block |

 If, for some reason, the resource data is arranged with the code block (containing the file data) before the component name, then the residual SIS file will be larger than necessary. 

## Installation

 Installation of an SIS file requires several steps to be performed. These are described in the following sections. 

 These operations need to be repeated for any embedded component SIS files. 

### Select Language

 SIS files may support more than one language, as indicated by the Number of languages field in the header and the language records. The control panel `Add/remove` program attempts to use the current language of the machine, but EPOC Connect prompts the user to choose from the available options. 

### Check Requisites

 The requisite records specify a list of other components that need to be installed. The residual SIS files on the target machine should be searched to verify that a suitable version of the required component has been installed.

...

### Copy Files

 The file records should be processed in the reverse of the order that they are stored in the SIS file. Text files should be displayed and component SIS files installed as they are encountered. 

 SIS files sometimes allow the user to select the installation drive. This is indicated by the destination file names having an exclamation mark ("`!`") specified as the drive letter. In this case the user should be prompted to select from the available drives. 

 Directories should be created automatically to accommodate files being copied. 

### Residual SIS File

 A residual SIS file is created in the `C:\System\Install\` directory on the target machine. This allows the control panel to display a list of installed programs, and provides the dependency information required for removing the component or installing other applications. 

 The main modification is that the file is truncated after the file name and component name strings. This usually means that the file data is omitted, but this relies upon the SIS file contents being in a sensible order. 

 Finally, three fields in the header are modified with the settings used for the installation. The Installation language field is set to the language selected for the installation, the Installation files field is set to the number of files installed, and the Installation drive field is set to the drive letter where the files were installed.

DumpSIS - Installation file decompiler in Software Installation Toolkit - reference

# `DumpSIS` - Installation file decompiler 

## Purpose

 `DumpSIS` is a PC-based utility which decompiles a SIS file. 

 The input to `DumpSIS` is a v9.x SIS file. Its output is the corresponding package file and (optionally) the source files. `CreateSIS` can be run on the resultant files to recreate the SIS file. When run on pre-v9.x SIS files, `DumpSIS` reports an error. 

 `DumpSIS` is found in the standard tools location, `\epoc32\tools\`. 

## Syntax

`> DumpSIS [-i] [-v] [-h] [-x] [-l[-y]][-d directory]
 filename.sis`

 where: 

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-i` | displays verbose output |
| `-v` | displays the `DumpSIS` version number |
| `-h` | displays help |
| `-x` | extracts the files |
| `-d` | specifies the directory to which the files are extracted, creating it if necessary. By default, files are extracted to a directory with the same as the SIS file. |
| `-p` | pauses before finishing. |
| `-l` | lists the executables and their capabilities. It also verifies that the capabilities listed in the SIS file are the same as those in the executable(s). |
| `-y` | lists the executables and their capabilities, in the format supported by the `DumpInstallFileStatus` tool. This option must be specified with the `-l` option. |

## Notes 

- The source-filenames specified in the original package file are not stored in the SIS file so `DumpSIS` invents names for the extracted files. 
- `DumpSIS` does not reinstate timestamps. 
- If the SIS file is signed, you can display and strip the signatures with `SignSIS`; `DumpSIS` makes no attempt to preserve or display any signing information.

## [Symbian OS v9.X - SIS File Format Specification](https://www.cryer.co.uk/file-types/s/sis/softwareinstallsis.pdf)

#### 1.1 Purpose and Scope

This document describes the newly restructured and redesigned SIS file format, which is introduced to 
complement the Symbian OS v9.1 release of Software Install. SIS files are used as the primary means of 
packaging files for deployment to a device, and are interpreted accordingly by the native software 
installer. As well as simply containing files, the SIS file can contain conditional statements which 
influence the installation e.g. device specific installations, language-specific installations, and user 
selectable optional components. 
Symbian OS v9.1 delivers new security features to the device, so operations which were previously 
possible via software install may now no-longer be possible. In addition, the device-side native installer is 
now policing the installation to ensure that the package meets certain security criteria before installation 
can succeed.

...

#### 2.1 Overview

The information in the SIS file is split up into two separate parts. The first part is the meta-data, 
describing the files that need to be installed. The second part of the SIS file contains all the actual file 
data. This enables software installation to be split into two phases, a decision and an installation phase. 
During the decision phase, the SIS file is examined and security checks are carried out in order to verify 
the install. The installation phase is only carried out if the verification is successful and is the process of 
copying the files to the device. 
2.1.1 Note on Reservation of SIS Field Values 
Please note that Symbian reserves the right to extend the set of applicable values relating to defined SIS 
fields, for example, fields employing bit-indicators such as TInstallFlags. 

The generation of unspecified values – outside the context of the supported MakeSIS and/or SignSIS tools is therefore likely to cause compatibility problems with later versions of Symbian OS. This may mean, therefore, that packages will fail to install.

#### 2.2 Integrity

The SIS file format supports signatures and certificates to enable a package to be signed. These 
signatures are verified during installation, and can also be re-verified after the package is installed on the 
device. 
In order to support the processing of the SIS file in two phases, only the meta-data of the SIS file is 
signed. The metadata contains hashes for each file in the package, in order to ensure the integrity of the 
file data, and therefore the integrity of the entire SIS file is protected by the signed meta-data. This 
means that during the installation phase software install can verify the hash against the one included in 
the signed meta-data for each file being installed, whilst using an untrusted component to perform any 
necessary decompression. 
Separate checksums for each of the meta-data and the file data are present in the SIS file to enable 
corrupt SIS files to be detected at the beginning of the installation process. These checksums are 
optional.

...

Since each SISField has a specified length, when parsing a SIS file the installer will ignore fields with unknown types.

...

#### 2.7 Programming Considerations

## [SIS/SISX package extraction, E32Image binary analysis ...](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/3612)
Published: 2026-10-14T18:47:32.000Z

Symbian OS (spanning EPOC, Series 60 / S60 v1-v5, UIQ, Series 80, and Symbian^3 / Anna / Belle) powers a vast historical ecosystem of mobile software, utilities, games, and enterprise tools. While official online services and vendor signing portals have ceased operations, the Symbian platform remains actively analyzed in retro-computing, digital preservation, embedded systems research, and mobile software forensics.

Currently, REA has no support for Symbian application containers, binary formats, or OS-specific C++ conventions. This feature introduces dedicated static reverse engineering capabilities for Symbian OS applications: unpacking `.sis` and `.sisx` package archives, parsing and loading E32Image executables/DLLs in Ghidra and Rizin, and reconstructing Symbian-specific architectural idioms (Cleanup Stack, Active Objects, Descriptors, and Capability security manifests).

### 1. Package Unpacking & Manifest Analysis (.sis and .sisx)

- Legacy SIS (Symbian v6–v8.x): Parse EPOC SIS archive headers, file records, language tables, and target drive mappings (`!:\system\apps\`).
- SISX / SIS9 (Symbian OS v9+):

- Parse the PKCS#7 signed SISX container, extracting embedded certificates, signatures, and trust chains.
- Extract package metadata: Package UID, Vendor Name, Target Device / S60 SDK compatibility ranges, and localized install manifests.
- Extract target file trees (e.g. `!:\sys\bin\*.exe`, `!:\resource\apps\*.rsc`, `!:\private\ \`).
- Map Capability Manifests: parse declared capabilities (e.g. `NetworkServices`, `LocalServices`, `ReadUserData`, `WriteUserData`, `UserEnvironment`, `DiskAdmin`, `AllFiles`, `TCB`) required by the application.

## [SIS / SISX (Symbian) file format — extraction guide and software | Archive Explorer](https://archiveexplorer.com/formats/sis-symbian)

SIS (and signed SISX) is the installer format for Symbian — once the largest mobile OS in the world. Nokia and Sony Ericsson phones installed apps as .sis files for two decades. Symbian shipped its last device in 2012, so SIS is now a historical curiosity.

...

## How to extract a SIS / SISX (Symbian) file

Opening a `.sis` file is straightforward on every modern operating system. The exact steps depend on which platform you are on:

### On Windows

1. Locate the `.sis` file in File Explorer.
2. Right-click the file. If you have 7-Zip installed, choose 7-Zip → Extract Here. On Windows 11 the built-in extractor handles ZIP, 7z, RAR and several other formats directly through Extract All…
3. If prompted, pick a destination folder and click Extract.
4. The extracted files appear in a folder next to the original archive.

### On macOS

1. Find the `.sis` file in Finder.
2. Install The Unarchiver from the Mac App Store, or Keka for both creating and extracting.
3. Right-click the file → Open With → The Unarchiver (or just double-click after Unarchiver is set as the default).
4. The extracted folder appears next to the archive.

### On Linux

1. Use your file manager: right-click the archive → Extract Here (file-roller on GNOME, Ark on KDE).
2. On the command line, run one of: 

```
7z x archive.sis    # works for almost any format
```
3. The files appear in the current directory.

...

## Technical details

SIS / SISX (Symbian) uses the DEFLATE algorithm and is identified on disk by the magic byte sequence `7A 1F 11 10`. The standard MIME type is `application/vnd.symbian.install`. The format is a proprietary specification and is free for any use.

...

### Is SIS / SISX (Symbian) safe to open?

Archive files are containers — they are only as safe as what they contain. A `.sis` from a trusted source is fine; one received from a stranger can hold malicious executables, scripts, or files engineered to exploit bugs in your archiver. Always keep your archiver updated, and never run unknown executables that come out of an archive. A safe workflow is to extract into a sandbox and scan the contents before opening anything.

The header of EPOC release 6 format SIS files is extended:

## File Records

 The Files pointer field in the header points to the file records that specify the details of the files to be installed. The Number of Files field in the header specifies the number of records. These are stored contiguously, in the reverse of the order required for installation. Each record starts with a 4 byte File record type field specifying the type of record that follows: 

| Type | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `0x00000000` | Simple file line |
| `0x00000001` | Multiple language files line |
| `0x00000002` | Options line |
| `0x00000003` | If line |
| `0x00000004` | ElseIf line |
| `0x00000005` | Else line |
| `0x00000006` | EndIf line |

...

If the File record type field at the start of the record is `0x00000000` or `0x00000001` then the record specifies a single file to be installed. It is in the following format: 

| Offset | | Bytes | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0x00` | 0 | 4 | File record type |
| `0x04` | 4 | 4 | File type |
| `0x08` | 8 | 4 | File details |
| `0x0c` | 12 | 4 | Source name length |
| `0x10` | 16 | 4 | Source name pointer |
| `0x14` | 20 | 4 | Destination name length |
| `0x18` | 24 | 4 | Destination name pointer |
| `0x1c` | 28 | 4 n | File length(s) |
| `0x1c` + 4 n | 28 + 4 n | 4 n | File pointer(s) |

 The file records of EPOC release 6 format SIS files are extended: 

| Offset | | Bytes | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0x1c` + 8 n | 28 + 8 n | 4 n | Original file length(s) |
| `0x1c` + 12 n | 28 + 12 n | 4 | MIME type length |

Unless otherwise specified the following conventions apply: 

- Numeric values larger than a byte are stored with the least significant byte first. 
- Strings are not terminated; their length is explicitly specified. 
- Pointers are specified as offsets from the start of the SIS file.

| `0x38` | 56 | 4 | Requisites pointer |

...

It is in the following format: 

| Offset | | Bytes | Description |

The File length and File pointer specify the length and offset of the file contents respectively. The Original file length specifies the size of the file when uncompressed. If the File record type field specifies that there are multiple language versions, then the File length, File pointer and Original file length fields are individually repeated for each language version supported by the SIS file. These are specified in the same order as the language records.

## Resource Data

 The remainder of the SIS file consists of the data referenced from the other sections. This is stored uncompressed and unpadded, usually in the following order: 

| Section |
| --- |
| String Block, containing: File Names Requisite Name Component Name |
| Code Block |
| Signature Block |

 If, for some reason, the resource data is arranged with the code block (containing the file data) before the component name, then the residual SIS file will be larger than necessary.

## Objective
- Recreate the supplied *Barakel: The Fallen Angel* game as an Android-playable game, matching the original as closely as feasible.

## Requirements
- “Make a game from the attached file which can be played on android. Make an exact copy of the game from the attached file.”

## Decisions
- The request supersedes the existing game’s original dark-fantasy interpretation; use the supplied game file as the reference.

## Work State
### Completed
- Confirmed the attachment is a Symbian EPOC Release 6 SIS installer; `7z` does not recognize it.
- Found references identifying *Barakel* as a 2004/2005 N-Gage diagonal-down action RPG by StormBASIC Games, published by Technobubble Entertainment.
- Located embedded path strings naming game files, including `BARAKEL.APP`, `Barakel.dat`, `barakel.mbm`, `Barakel.cfg`, and `techno1.sbi`.

### Active
- Correctly parse and extract the SIS contents to inspect assets and gameplay data.
- Use those findings to adapt and test the existing Android-playable browser game.

### Blocked
- SIS file records have not yet been parsed or extracted; an exploratory script incorrectly assumed fixed-width records and produced invalid output.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the legacy EPOC 6 SIS layout and correctly parse this installer’s variable-length records, file sizes, pointers, and compressed contents.
2. Extract and inspect the game’s asset and data files, especially `.mbm`, `.dat`, `.cfg`, and `.sbi`.
3. Compare original gameplay and visuals with `index.html`, then improve fidelity and test at a mobile-sized viewport.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/uploads/4f4c6aff-6761-4fca-adce-b9b4ef543800/barakel_-_the_fallen_angel_n-gage-138572.sis`: supplied game installer.
- `index.html`: existing playable Three.js browser game.
- `/tmp/opencode/pysisextract/sisfile.py`: reference parser for newer SIS format; its documentation says it does not target this legacy format.
- `/tmp/opencode/sisinfo/`: SIS inspection project, but its documentation likewise describes newer SIS/SISX formats.

## Important Context
- Repository changes are uncommitted.
- SIS size is 6,308,757 bytes; header indicates 13 files. The embedded paths target `!:\system\apps\Barakel\`.
- SIS format notes found via web search: EPOC Release 6 file records are variable-sized and may include multiple file lengths/pointers; file data is zlib-compressed unless the `NC` option is set.

content.text:
antirez weblog
rss / about / it

Sisopen - epoc and symbian file extraction utility

Sisopen

Sisopen is a tool to list and extract the content of SIS files. SIS files are installation files used in Symbian-based smartphones like many S60 Nokia phones.

Sisopen is an ANSI-C program, mainly targetted to Linux and other Unix-like systems it can be compiled almost in every system with a C compiler having zlib.

Defining NOZLIB at compile time makes you able to compile without zlib, but only file listing is available in this mode, files can't be extracted.

EXAMPLE

First example, list the content of a .sis file 
$ sisopen sis/torch.sis

sis/torch.sis: SIS header detected
  application UID: 0x78F172C
  application version: 1.20

Languages
  UK English 

Files
000   !:\system\apps\Torch\Torch.aif                                        1941
001   !:\system\apps\Torch\Torch_caption.rsc                                  32
002   !:\system\apps\Torch\Torch.rsc                                          70
003   !:\system\apps\Torch\Torch.app                                        5548
A more interesting example showing the ability of sisopen to fully understand SIS files including conditionals: 
$ sisopen sis/Nokia_N70_patch.SIS

sis/Nokia_N70_patch.SIS: SIS header detected
  application UID: 0x20000BB0
  application version: 1.00

Languages
  UK English 

Files
[endif]
001 f C:\DOCUME~1\m1smith\LOCALS~1\Temp\MKS0\WrongDevice0.txt                122
[else]
003 f C:\DOCUME~1\m1smith\LOCALS~1\Temp\MKS0\Finished0.txt                   254
004 c C:\system\temp\NokiaN70Patch1.exe                                     1552
005 f C:\DOCUME~1\m1smith\LOCALS~1\Temp\MKS0\Distribution0.txt               288
[if (0x10200f9a == MachineUID)]
SIS file conditionals must be read upside down, starting from the bottom of the output. This is a patch for the N70 smartphone so the conditional is if MachineUID == 0x... (the N70 UID) install the files, else show a Wrong Device message.

FEATURES

Sisopen is able to:
  • list SIS file content, including conditionals, file type, installation time options
  • extract files (try -x)
  • the verbose mode gives a lot more information about the sis header and individual files (try -v)

DOWNLOAD

sisopen-0.1.tar.gz

for compilation instructions read the README file inside the tar.gz

AUTHOR & CREDITS

Sisopen was written by Salvatore Sanfilippo (antirez at gmail dot com) using the documentation describing the SIS format written by Alexander Thoukydides (alex at thouky dot co dot uk) available at http://homepage.ntlworld.com/thouky/software/psifs/sis.html

CONTACTS, PATCHES, ...

Please write an email to antirez at gmail dot com for patches, suggestions, bug reports.

Have fun, Salvatore Sanfilippo

5: smartphones like many S60 Nokia phones.
6: 
7: SYSTEMS WHERE SYSOPEN CAN RUN
8: 
9: Sisopen is an ANSI-C program, mainly targetted to Linux and other
10: Unix-like systems it can be compiled almost in every system with
11: a C compiler having zlib.
12: 
13: COMPILING SISOPEN

24: 
25: Defining NOZLIB at compile time makes you able to compile without
26: zlib, but only file listing is available in this mode, files
27: can't be extracted.

## [GBX.ru -> [N-Gage] Игры от StormBasic.](https://gbx.ru/?showtopic=128673)

[N-Gage] Игры от StormBasic., Barakel, TechWars, PoolFriction, FS MotoCross.

| lps | Воскресенье, 04 марта 2018, 13:19 Отправлено #1 |
| --- | --- |
| у меня всё хорошо Группа: Пользователи Сообщений: 2 958 Регистрация: 11 мая. 2008 Из: Крым, Симферополь Пользователь №: 26 686 | Наверняка все помнят рпг Barakel - The Fallen Angel, ситуация с которой мне не совсем понятна. Игра позиционировалась, как N-Gage и для запуска на других смартфонах нуждалась в установке фиксов от wl. Однако официально она выходила на испанском и патч-англофикатор приходилось накатывать сверху и я не припоминаю чтобы нокийцы подтверждали её (если не так - поправьте). Кроме того, от них же на закате 6-8 симбы выходило ещё как минимум 2 игры и обе тоже на испанском: TechWars и Freestyle Moto Coss, которые тоже нужно было фиксить под более свежие версии Symbian. С переводом на английский ситуация аналогичная, делили его энтузиасты. Сам перевод, всех трёх игр был сделан "в лоб", т.е. текст тупо перебивался в hex-редакторе так, чтобы уместиться в длину оригинальной строки, а если перевод короче оригинала, то до нужной длины добивался пробелами. Короче, то ещё "качество", но другого не имели. » Нажмите, для открытия спойлера « QUOTE (eskander @ Воскресенье, 04 марта 2018, 15:24) По StormBasic игры переводили не абстрактные "фанаты", а один конкретный человек: StormBasic.MotoCross.FreeStyle.NGAGE.Translated.to.English-ANiMeX StormBasic.TechWars.Translated.in.English.NGAGE-ANiMeX Но переводы да, далеки от идеала. Касательно Баракеля, его доработал Богдан "BodyZ", в том числе там устранена одна критическая ошибка. Ещё он перевёл на EN PoolFriction. Касательно ситуации с играми от StormBasic в целом, я уже писал, это что-то вроде half'офф. игр. Они не входили в как таковое семейство N-Gage проектов, но продавались в Испании на картриджах вложенных в комплект (как бандл) с некоторыми изданиями N-Gage QD. Все эти игры были разработаны именно исходно под N-Gage и продавались _только_ в вышеупомянутых бандлах. Запуск на остальных аппаратах, это уже всё сторонние фиксы. ## [SBI Files](https://psxdatacenter.com/sbifiles.html)

Sony first introduced LibCrypt protection in PAL version of MediEvil in October 1998. Since then more than hundred games containing LibCrypt have been released. What's special about this protection is that it uses subchannels to store some non-Yellow Book data, thus breaking the standard. SBI Files are archives that contains the protection information that those PAL games got and that are needed to run those protected games in emulators. The games themselves will never be available here, so please don't ask for games. I want to thank the people of the redump (http://redump.org) for all their work making these sbi files. HOW TO USE SBI FILES: 1 - Download the sbi file or files that are for the original game that you got. 2 - Extract them in the patches folder of epsxe.

## Description 

Barakel, an exterminating angel has been banished from the Sky World and sent to the human world for insubordination. Hoping to redeem himself, the fallen angel seeks the help of magician to cleanse the souls of sinners. The player navigates Barakel from a 3D overhead view travelling to new places, fighting enemies, talking to people, casting some spells at his disposal and collecting items. There are some RPG elements that allow Barakel to gain experience and levels to raise his Health Points and Magic Points as well as equip items and acquire gold for purchases.

...

## [Barakel: The Fallen Angel (N-Gage) | JRK's RPGs](https://jrkrpg.pl/gry/ngage/barakel-the-fallen-angel/)

# Barakel: The Fallen Angel

Wydania

 2004() 2004() 2004() 

Ogólnie

RPG akcji w postaci brawlera fabularnego w settingu fantasy, bazującego mocno na aspektach losowości wypadających przedmiotów i zdolności gracza na wychodzenie z potyczek z jak najmniejszymi stratami. Wydany tylko w Iberii, ale z wbudowanym językiem angielskim.

Widok

izometr

Walka

czas rzeczywisty

...

Ze względu na to że gra jest stosunkowo nieznana, to na parę słów wstępu warto przytoczyć że Barakel jest grą wydaną ekskluzywnie na portugalski i hiszpański market, jest raczej niedostępna poza tym rynkiem. Mimo że to dosyć niszowy tytuł, miał grono wielbicieli, a nawet doczekał sie amatorskiego tłumaczenia na język angielski. Niestety tłumaczenie na język angielski stworzyło pewną niedogodność, a mianowicie gra ładuje mapki obszarów bazując na tych samych nazwach co są wyświetlane w dialogach, a co za tym szło, do pewnej lokacji nie da się wejść w angielskiej wersji bo gra się po prostu wysypuje. Na szczęście pliki zapisu są kompatybilne z oryginalną wersją gry i przejście kłopotliwej lokacji można dokonać w portugalskiej wersji, a po ukończeniu lokacji przekopiować pliki i się z powrotem na angielską przełączyć.

...

Graficznie jest nawet dosyć dobrze, cała gra jest w 3D, w którym kamera z pewnej wysokości podąża za graczem. Modele wyglądają ok jak na możliwości N-Gage. Obecnie odpalenie gry chociażby na emulatorze nie sprawia zbytnio zachwycającego wrażenia. Trzeba mieć tu jednak na uwadze, że N-Gage bazowało na rozdzielczościach 176x208, mimo że gra wygląda słabo na pierwszy rzut oka, to pomniejszona do właściwych rozdzielczości platformy na które została tworzona, to wygląda już całkiem solidnie. Mimo wszystko, wszelkie gry stworzone w 3D na początku lat dwutysięcznych zdecydowanie się źle zestarzały i w przypadku Barakela nie jest inaczej. Za jedną sprawę jednak musze grę pochwalić, a mianowicie ekwipowane bronie i tarcze są faktycznie reprezentowane na modelu postaci. Kolejną sprawą jest płynność działania, z którą jest ogólnie bardzo dobrze, walka nawet z kilkoma przeciwnikami naraz działa płynnie, nawet jak kilku przeciwników miota w nas pociskami nie zauważyłem istotnych zwolnień rozgrywki. Ku memu zdziwieniu jedyne dosyć mocne przymulenie gry następuje w mieście gdzie nie ma losowych przeciwników ani żadnych latających pocisków. Zapewne jest to spowodowane renderowaniem bardziej złożonych obiektów w mieście, bo w rejonach gdzie atakują nas wrogowie mamy z reguły dosyć otwartą przestrzeń z małą ilością obiektów otoczenia. To mnie naprowadza na kolejną sprawę, poruszając się poza miastem mamy sporo pustej przestrzeni, nie spodziewajcie się tu jakieś zawiłej aranżacji przestrzeni, tu pojawi się jakaś czaszka na podłodze, a tam w kącie pochodnia i tyle. Coś za coś, wystrój podziemi Jest minimalistyczny, ale jest funkcjonalne i gra nie traci dynamiki podczas potyczek.

...

Gra jest typowym Action-RPG gdzie rozgrywka toczy się w czasie rzeczywistym. Wszelkie potyczki są generowane losowo i w momencie pojawienia się przeciwników zostaniemy uwięzieni w pewnej przestrzeni aktualnej lokacji. Nie ma możliwości uciekania z potyczek, tylko pokonanie przeciwników umożliwi podążanie dalej, co daje wrażenie troszkę takiego brawlera (Beat-Em-Upa) 3D podczas rozgrywki. Nasza postać ma zestaw dwóch sekwencji kombosów, które wykonujemy automatycznie szybko wciskając ten sam klawisz podczas konkretnych animacji ataku. Ma to pewną wadę, bo jeśli postać wykonuje sekwencję ciosów to przestaje reagować na próbę poruszenia się, w wyniku czego często oberwiemy gdy przyjdzie nam walczyć z więcej niż jednym wrogiem. Można tego uniknąć obserwując naszą broń i wyczekiwać momentu aż jej pozycja wróci do bazowej, bo jeśli nie wciśniemy kolejnego klawisza do końca animacji ciosu, to postać nie przełączy się w tryb sekwencji ciosów, dzięki czemu możemy efektywnie w pewnym rytmie zadawać kolejne ciosy z zachowaniem mobilności, gdzie trzeba będzie się odsunąć przed ciosem wroga. Z względu na to że gra jest dosyć ciężka, a możliwości naszej postaci dosyć ograniczone, to będzie właśnie takiego min-maxingu od nas wymagać, byśmy wyszukiwali każdej przewagi jaką możemy tylko dostać. Oprócz bazowego machania bronią możemy jeszcze blokować ataki wyekwipowaną tarczą, a w późniejszym etapie gry również rzucać zaklęcia. W kwestii zaklęć zdecydowanie zabrakło mi magii leczącej, znalazłem tylko trzy sposoby do leczenia mojej postaci, a było to przez napoiki życia, wbicie poziomu, a również przez zakupienie napoika życia u czarodziejki. Często idąc na zakupy, kupowałem tylko pojedynczo napoik, by stoczyć co najmniej jedną walkę więcej na obecnym zregenerowanym życiu, bo o zasoby może bywać naprawdę ciężko podczas rozgrywki, szczególnie że wszelki drop jest w pełni losowy, a przedmiotów nie da się sprzedawać. A teraz warto wspomnieć, że gra ogólnie zapisuje progresję jak wychodzimy z gry, ale by zabezpieczyć swoją progresje przed śmiercią postaci trzeba kupić napój odrodzenia, co jest formą zapisu pozwalającego nam startować z danego miejsca po każdej śmierci. Jedną z pozytywnych rzeczy to wbudowany questlog, w menu postaci, jedną z zakładek stanowi opis naszego aktualnego zadania, co dobrze mieć zawsze do sprawdzenia. 

Kwestia rozwoju postaci jest tu zautomatyzowana, nasza postać zdobywa doświadczenie dzięki któremu dobija kolejne poziomy. Nasz bohater jest opisany tylko dwoma podstawowymi statystykami, a mianowicie punktami życia i magii, które rosną z poziomem. Poza tym jako statystykę można by uznać sam poziom, bo to według niego wszystko skaluje. Zależnie od poziomu, wrogowie będą nam upuszczali więcej złota, lepszy ekwipunek, ale również będziemy napotykać więcej i silniejszych wrogów oraz ceny przedmiotów i usług będą rosnąć. Jest to dosyć cwane rozwiązanie, bo jak się na to spojrzy obiektywnie, to gra w ten sposób zwiększa nam siłę i obronę, bez potrzeby stosowania osobnej statystyki siły i obrony. I tu jest pewna kwestia, która może zepsuć nam rozgrywkę, a mianowicie wysoka losowość dropu. Grając mamy ograniczony czas na zdobycie nowego ekwipunku, ponieważ wszelkie bronie i tarcze mają współczynnik wytrzymałości. Gdy gra staje się niełaskawa co do wypadających przedmiotów, to możemy skończyć kompletnie bez zasobów i to z rozlatującym sie ekwipunkiem w dłoniach. W tej sytuacji, nawet gdyby nasz ekwipunek dłużej wytrzymał, to nadal stoimy z wyższym poziomem przeciwko większej ilości jeszcze silniejszych przeciwników, czyniąc rozgrywkę drastyczną walką o przetrwanie do następnego dropu. W kwestiach samego ekwipunku, to mamy do dyspozycji 4 sloty, 3 są dostępne na broń, tarczę i zaklęcie, a czwarty slot jest automatycznie zapełniany przez napoiki życia, których można mieć maksymalnie 9. Następnie mamy nasz inwentarz w którym możemy trzymać 8 przedmiotów w zapasie. Wyjątek stanowią tu napoiki MP, które można stackować do 9 sztuk na każdy jeden z ośmiu slotów, czyli możemy ich mieć maksymalnie 72, jeśli się zdecydujemy wypełnić nimi inwentarz. W kwestii samego ekwipunku, to mamy do dyspozycji całą gamę różnorodnie wyglądających tarcz, jednak bronie bym podzielił tylko na 4 typy. Małe i duże miecze oraz małe i duże siekiery. Różnice można zobaczyć wizualnie i impaktowo, konkretne bronie będą miały większy model wizualny w ręce gracza i nieco lepszy zasięg. Różnica między siekierami a mieczami jest typowa jak dla gier RPG, siekiery mają tendencje do szerokiego rozproszenia zadawanych obrażeń przy nieco wolniejszym machaniu nią, a miecze mają bardziej zawężony zakres obrażeń przy nieco szybciejszym machaniu bronią.

...

W całej grze wypadły mi trzy różne zaklęcia, niszczenie nieumarłych, piorun raniący wszystko w naszym pobliżu i ogień raniący wszystko na polu walki, ale za to nieco słabiej niż piorun. Warto wspomnieć że gra ma dziwną tendencję pozwolenia graczowi rzucenia zaklęcia gdy mamy za mało MP na to, a co za tym idzie, w menu zobaczymy nasze MP na ujemnym poziomie, gdzie przestrzegałbym przed wychodzeniem na inną mapę z ujemną wartością MP, bo gra może się po prostu wyłączyć. A nawet jakby mapka się poprawnie załadowała, to już widać w konsoli emulatora jak tam zaczynają lecieć jakieś ciągłe błędy. Na szczęście stojąc w miejscu nasze MP będzie stopniowo się samo regenerować, więc w razie potrzeby można odczekać jakieś 40 sekund by jednak mieć te MP ponad 0 i spokojnie ruszać dalej.

...

Tak więc mamy tu do czynienia z RPGiem akcji w postaci brawlera fabularnego w settingu fantasy, bazującego mocno na aspektach losowości wypadających przedmiotów i zdolności gracza na wychodzenie z potyczek z jak najmniejszymi stratami. Rozgrywka może być bardzo frustrująca, bo mimo zrobienia wszystkiego dobrze, możemy skończyć bez zasobów z rozpadającą się bronią, a ubijanie przeciwników gołymi pięściami ciągnie się w nieskończoność, tak jakby się okładało w pojedynkę bossa raidowego w jakimś MMO. Jeśli jednak gracz nauczy się sekwencji walki z poszczególnymi przeciwnikami i odpowiednio zaplanuje przeznaczenie swoich zasobów, to gra daje ogromną uciechę z progresji. Jak to z reguły bywa, że sporemu poziomowi frustracji towarzyszy sporo uciechy jak w końcu da się radę. Grę bym nie polecił każdemu, ale taki fan Diablo z sporą tolerancją na nisko rozdzielczościową pikselozę obiektów 3D, znalazłby w niej z pewnością sporo uciechy, a szczególnie że gra jest raczej krótka. Gdy wiemy co robić, gdzie czego szukać i bogowie RNG nam sprzyjają co do wypadających przedmiotów, można ją ukończyć delikatnie w jakieś 3-4 godziny. 

Zalety: + Dobre dźwięki oręża + Niby duża frustracja a jednak spora satysfakcja + Bronie i tarcze są wizualnie pokazywane na modelu postaci + Quest log

Wady: - Mały wpływ gracza na rozwój postaci - Frustracja losowości dropu - Brak możliwości sprzedawania przedmiotów - Mało typów broni - Bezużyteczna mapka - Bug z MP który może wysypać grę - Ceny usług i napoi rosną z poziomem

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Recreate *Barakel: The Fallen Angel* from the supplied game file as an Android-playable game, matching the original as closely as feasible.

## Requirements
- “Make a game from the attached file which can be played on android. Make an exact copy of the game from the attached file.”

## Decisions
- Use the supplied game as the reference rather than the existing game’s original dark-fantasy interpretation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Identified the attachment as an EPOC Release 6 SIS installer for *Barakel: The Fallen Angel*.
- Extracted the installer and parsed its StormCE VFS data container; 333 embedded files were extracted, including `.sbi` graphics assets and game data.
- Decoded SBI image data and generated PNG previews in `/tmp/opencode/previews/`.

### Active
- Inspect the original assets and gameplay data, then compare them with the existing browser game and improve fidelity.
- Test the Android-playable game at a mobile-sized viewport.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the generated original-game image previews and extracted data.
2. Compare the original presentation and gameplay with `index.html`; update the game toward the reference.
3. Test the result at a mobile-sized viewport.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/uploads/4f4c6aff-6761-4fca-adce-b9b4ef543800/barakel_-_the_fallen_angel_n-gage-138572.sis`: supplied installer.
- `/tmp/opencode/barakel-extract/`: SIS-extracted game files, including `Barakel.dat` and `Barakel.cfg`.
- `/tmp/opencode/barakel-vfs/`: 333 files extracted from the StormCE VFS container.
- `/tmp/opencode/previews/`: decoded PNG previews of selected SBI image assets.
- `index.html`: existing Three.js browser game to adapt.

## Important Context
- The SIS contains `BARAKEL.APP`, `Barakel.dat`, `barakel.mbm`, `Barakel.cfg`, and `techno1.sbi`; embedded install paths target `!:\system\apps\Barakel\`.
- SBI files start with an `iiii` header; image payloads are zlib-compressed from byte offset 20. The extracted archive includes 176×208 title/menu artwork and 64×64 hero sprites.
- Repository changes are uncommitted; the existing game is currently titled *ASHEN CROWN* and uses a custom 3D sanctuary, shards, wraiths, and touch controls.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Recreate *Barakel: The Fallen Angel* from the supplied game file as an Android-playable game, matching the original as closely as feasible.

## Requirements
- “Make a game from the attached file which can be played on android. Make an exact copy of the game from the attached file.”

## Decisions
- Use the supplied game as the reference rather than the existing game’s original dark-fantasy interpretation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Identified the attachment as an EPOC Release 6 SIS installer for *Barakel: The Fallen Angel*.
- Extracted the installer and parsed its StormCE VFS data container; 333 embedded files were extracted, including `.sbi` graphics assets and game data.
- Decoded SBI image data and generated PNG previews for selected assets in `/tmp/opencode/previews/`.

### Active
- Inspect original assets and gameplay data, then compare them with the existing browser game and improve fidelity.
- Test the Android-playable game at a mobile-sized viewport.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `/tmp/opencode/previews/` and the extracted data for the original game's presentation and gameplay.
2. Compare the reference with `index.html`; update the game toward the original.
3. Test the result at a mobile-sized viewport.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/uploads/4f4c6aff-6761-4fca-adce-b9b4ef543800/barakel_-_the_fallen_angel_n-gage-138572.sis`: supplied installer.
- `/tmp/opencode/barakel-extract/`: SIS-extracted game files, including `Barakel.dat` and `Barakel.cfg`.
- `/tmp/opencode/barakel-vfs/`: 333 files extracted from the StormCE VFS container.
- `/tmp/opencode/previews/`: decoded PNG previews of selected SBI assets.
- `index.html`: existing Three.js browser game, currently titled *ASHEN CROWN* and using a custom 3D sanctuary, shards, wraiths, and touch controls.

## Important Context
- SIS install paths target `!:\system\apps\Barakel\`; extracted files include `BARAKEL.APP`, `Barakel.dat`, `barakel.mbm`, `Barakel.cfg`, and `techno1.sbi`.
- `Barakel.dat` contains a 28-byte entry table with 333 records; embedded assets include 176×208 title/menu artwork and 64×64 hero sprites.
- SBI files start with an `iiii` header; image payloads are zlib-compressed from byte offset 20. The SBI formats observed include grayscale `0x801` and RGB `0x1801`.

==== PO.Intro.dat ====
--------------------------------------------------
------- P6 Languaje File:10:28 06/08/2004 --------
--------------------------------------------------
Escuta atencioso, mortal, o relato que narrarei a seguir, pois só uns poucos privilegiados têm ocasião de escutá-lo...
A nossa história começa faz muito tempo, quando um anjo exterminador chamado Barakel negou-se a cumprir um mandato divino que ordenava-lhe ceifar inumeráveis vidas.

from pathlib import Path
import struct,zlib

def png(path,w,h,data,channels):
 ctype={1:0,3:2,4:6}[channels]
 rows=b''.join(b'\0'+data[y*w*channels:(y+1)*w*channels] for y in range(h))
 def chunk(tag,body):return struct.pack('>I',len(body))+tag+body+struct.pack('>I',zlib.crc32(tag+body)&0xffffffff)
 out=b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n'+chunk(b'IHDR',struct.pack('>IIBBBBB',w,h,8,ctype,0,0,0))+chunk(b'IDAT',zlib.compress(rows))+chunk(b'IEND',b'')
 Path(path).write_bytes(out)
for name in ['gHero','gHeroLow0','gHeroLow1','gSkeleton0','gDarkWarrior0','gAxeWarrior2','gMenu','logo','GameOver']:

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Recreate *Barakel: The Fallen Angel* from the supplied game file as an Android-playable game, matching the original as closely as feasible.

## Requirements
- “Make a game from the attached file which can be played on android. Make an exact copy of the game from the attached file.”

## Decisions
- Use the supplied game as the reference rather than the existing game’s original dark-fantasy interpretation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Identified the attachment as an EPOC Release 6 SIS installer for *Barakel: The Fallen Angel*.
- Extracted the installer and parsed its StormCE VFS data container; 333 embedded files were extracted, including graphics, game data, and models.
- Decoded SBI image data and generated PNG previews for selected assets in `/tmp/opencode/previews/`.
- Inspected English game text and map data: the original is a third-person fantasy RPG with a village map, movement, running, attack, defense, spells, potions, inventory, and multiple areas.
- Confirmed the repository’s `index.html` is a Three.js game titled *ASHEN CROWN*, with custom 3D sanctuary gameplay and touch controls; it has not yet been adapted to the reference.

### Active
- Inspect original assets and gameplay data, then compare them with `index.html` and improve fidelity.
- Test the Android-playable game at a mobile-sized viewport.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect previews and extracted model/map assets further to determine a feasible faithful browser-game presentation.
2. Update `index.html` toward the original game’s RPG setting and mechanics, replacing its unrelated sanctuary/shard/wraith premise.
3. Test the result at a mobile-sized viewport.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/uploads/4f4c6aff-6761-4fca-adce-b9b4ef543800/barakel_-_the_fallen_angel_n-gage-138572.sis`: supplied installer.
- `/tmp/opencode/barakel-extract/`: SIS-extracted installer contents, including `Barakel.dat` and `Barakel.cfg`.
- `/tmp/opencode/barakel-vfs/`: 333 extracted StormCE VFS files, including `.sbi`, `.md2`, `.dat`, and map assets.
- `/tmp/opencode/previews/`: decoded PNG previews and test decodes of original assets.

## Important Context
- SIS install paths target `!:\system\apps\Barakel\`; extracted files include `BARAKEL.APP`, `Barakel.dat`, `barakel.mbm`, `Barakel.cfg`, and `techno1.sbi`.

## Objective
- Recreate *Barakel: The Fallen Angel* from the supplied game file as an Android-playable game, matching the original as closely as feasible.

## Requirements
- “Make a game from the attached file which can be played on android. Make an exact copy of the game from the attached file.”

## Decisions
- Use the supplied game as the reference rather than the repository’s existing unrelated dark-fantasy game.
- Preserve extracted original graphics and MD2 models as local assets for the browser game.

## Work State
### Completed
- Identified the attachment as an EPOC Release 6 SIS installer for *Barakel: The Fallen Angel* and extracted its StormCE VFS contents.
- Inspected game text, village map exits, enemy/item definitions, and selected original image previews.
- Copied a selected set of decoded original PNG graphics and MD2 models into `assets/barakel/`.

### Active
- Adapt `index.html` from its current *ASHEN CROWN* sanctuary/shard gameplay into a closer representation of Barakel’s third-person fantasy RPG and original village setting.
- Integrate original assets where practical and test at a mobile-sized viewport.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the newly copied assets and the current `index.html` structure.
2. Replace the unrelated sanctuary premise and mechanics with Barakel-inspired RPG presentation and touch controls.
3. Run the game and verify it at a mobile viewport.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/uploads/4f4c6aff-6761-4fca-adce-b9b4ef543800/barakel_-_the_fallen_angel_n-gage-138572.sis`: supplied installer.
- `/tmp/opencode/barakel-vfs/`: 333 extracted StormCE VFS files, including original game assets and definitions.
- `/tmp/opencode/previews/`: decoded reference image previews.
- `assets/barakel/`: selected decoded PNG images and copied MD2 models for use in the game.

## Important Context
- Original controls include movement, double-click to run, attack, protect, spells, potions, and enemy targeting; inventory supports item use and throwing.
- Original story follows exiled angel Barakel seeking a magician who can cleanse souls, then fighting the King-Demon.
- `Def_Map1.dat` specifies village exits toward maps 2, 5, 7, and 11, and includes NPCs such as a witch, farmer, blacksmith, and aunt.
- The active repository game is currently a Three.js game with custom sanctuary gameplay; it is not yet adapted to Barakel.
- Changes are uncommitted; repository contains untracked project files including `index.html` and `assets/barakel/`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Recreate *Barakel: The Fallen Angel* from the supplied game file as an Android-playable game, matching the original as closely as feasible.

## Requirements
- “Make a game from the attached file which can be played on android. Make an exact copy of the game from the attached file.”

## Decisions
- Use the supplied game as the reference rather than the repository’s unrelated original game.
- Preserve and reuse decoded original graphics and MD2 models as local assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Identified the attachment as an EPOC Release 6 SIS installer and extracted its StormCE VFS contents.
- Inspected game text, village map exits, NPCs, enemies, items, and original image previews.
- Added selected decoded PNG graphics and MD2 models under `assets/barakel/`.
- Replaced `index.html` with a Barakel-themed game UI, mobile controls, intro, dialogue, inventory, and pause overlays.
- Added `style.css` with responsive HUD and touch-control layouts.
- Started `game.js` with Three.js setup, village scenery, original MD2 loading, and initial settlement props.

### Active
- Finish `game.js`; the file currently ends after constructing brazier props and has no gameplay loop, player/enemy actors, interaction logic, or control bindings.
- Replace fallback village props with original models where practical, and implement movement, NPC dialogue, combat, potions, quest progression, and mobile/keyboard controls.
- Run the game and verify it at a mobile-sized viewport.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `game.js` from the brazier setup; implement player, NPCs, model loading/animation, interactions, and gameplay loop.
2. Connect existing UI controls and keyboard input to movement, attack, guard, spell, potion, pause, inventory, and dialogue.
3. Run the game and check for console/runtime errors and mobile layout/control usability.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/uploads/4f4c6aff-6761-4fca-adce-b9b4ef543800/barakel_-_the_fallen_angel_n-gage-138572.sis`: supplied installer.
- `/tmp/opencode/barakel-vfs/`: extracted original game files and definitions.
- `/tmp/opencode/previews/`: decoded reference image previews.
- `assets/barakel/`: selected decoded original PNG graphics and copied MD2 models.
- `index.html`: revised Barakel game structure and HUD.
- `style.css`: responsive visual styling and touch controls.
- `game.js`: incomplete Three.js game implementation.

## Important Context
- Original controls include movement, double-click to run, attack, protect, spells, potions, and enemy targeting; inventory supports item use and throwing.
- The story follows exiled angel Barakel seeking a magician who can cleanse souls, then fighting the King-Demon.
- Original village data identifies exits to maps 2, 5, 7, and 11, and NPCs including a witch, farmer, blacksmith, and aunt.
- The current `game.js` has not yet been run or tested; copied MD2 assets may lack their original PCX skins.
